headline: On the Phase 4 noise basis the between-player variance is not positive in 4 of 4 cells (SNR -0.74 to -0.65), which reproduces the Phase 4 finding. That estimator divides a per-ball residual variance by a Kish count of equally sized MATCHES, so its noise term is larger than the sampling variance of a player mean by roughly the number of pressure balls per match. With the noise estimated as independent balls the estimate is positive in 4 of 4 cells and with match-cluster noise in 4 of 4. Those two bases bracket the truth (independent balls understate noise when balls inside a match are dependent, the cluster estimator is biased low with few matches per player), so the data cannot pin the size of tau2.

A model-free check agrees that some between-player signal exists: odd/even split-half reliability on the full pre-test window is estimable in 4 of 4 cells, with Spearman-Brown values from 0.25 to 0.42 (intervals in section 3). These are modest, and the intervals of several cells reach or cross zero. The statement 'signal-to-noise is at or below zero' is therefore mainly a property of the Phase 4 noise estimator, not proof that players do not differ under pressure. It is also not proof that the ranking is reliable. This is an open issue for review: the Phase 4 estimator is NOT changed here (methodology is not locked).
unresolved_issues: Noise model of the shrinkage estimator: the Phase 4 `n_eff` is a Kish count of equally sized matches but is divided into a per-ball variance. This drives the negative Phase 4 SNR and the strong shrinkage (floor hits, `shrink_tau4`). Choosing a different noise model changes every shrunk score and needs a decision before the methodology is locked.
The size of the between-player variance remains unidentified (brackets in section 2). Until it is identified, ranking reliability claims are not supportable.
Bowler pressure uses batter-state signals. Section 7 shows how three bowler-specific candidates behave; no candidate is adopted. Adopting one is a methodology decision.
Every eligibility threshold is still the unvalidated TRAIN-median working pool (20 / 16 / 49 / 29 balls).
Sample sizes are small in several cells (see player counts); intervals are wide and some cells are NOT_ESTIMABLE.

Date verification, strict capped/uncapped classification and the methodology-validation gate are unresolved (section 11). A later TEST evaluation is not a pristine hold-out because Phase 4 aggregate TEST results were shown.
